newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says govt sure to approve budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says govt sure to approve budget.

text.p: Italian prime minister Romano Prodi said on Saturday that he was sure the country's budget package for 1997 would be approved.

Prodi was responding to remarks by far-left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti who told a rally on Friday night that "at the moment, the government has a 50 percent chance" of getting the budget through.
Asked by reporters what chances he thought the government had, Prodi replied: "100 percent".
Bertinotti had said much depended on meetings in the next few days and again singled out privatisation plans, opposed by Refoundation, as a major sticking point.
A government source said on Friday that the government could have the budget ready for presentation to parliament as early as September 27.
The centre-left government aims to cut next year's public sector borrowing requirement by 32.4 trillion lire.
The package must be presented to parliament by September 30. Both chambers then have until December 31 to approve it.
